title: Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management: generative insights in Demand planning, with a trends metric at general availability
summary: The briefing correctly distinguishes the planned January 2027 release from the documented preview and accurately describes the tenant-level AI setting, licensing requirement and access controls. Minor corrections should identify the license-assignment request properties and attribute the user-role prerequisite to the security roles page.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: The Copilot enablement page lists no setting specific to generative insights.
claims.quote: Searched: "generative insights" "Demand planning" disable enable setting and "Demand planning" "generative insights" "disable"; read Enable Copilot capabilities and the feature page. The separate Copilot for demand planning setting is documented for Analyze demand plans, not this feature.

claims.where: Scope: Who; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Demand planning access requires a Power Platform account with the appropriate feature roles, including Demand Planning Contributor, Demand Planning Manager or System Administrator.
claims.quote: To be able to access Demand planning, users must sign in a Power Platform user account that has the security roles for the features they need.
claims.fix: In Scope: Who, replace 'the install page says users need the Power Platform roles for the features they use' with 'the security roles page says users need a Power Platform account with the security roles for the features they need'. The cited users-access page states this; the install page does not.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Scope: Who
claims.claim: Contributors without Demand Planning Manager or System Administrator can view and edit only data granted through row-level access rules.
claims.quote: Users who have the Demand Planning Contributor role (but not Demand Planning Manager or System Administrator) can access Demand planning, but they can only view and edit data that they're granted access to.

claims.claim: Some detailed insight graphs show dimension breakdowns identifying contributing products or locations.
claims.quote: Some detailed graphs provide a dimension breakdown that lets you review the major contributors to the detected insights. For example, you can see which products or locations contributed most

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions

claims.quote: Searched: "generative insights" "Demand planning" "row-level" "Feature management"; read the feature page, FAQ and users-access. The feature page describes dimension breakdowns but does not discuss row-level security or contributor-specific insight views.

claims.claim: The FAQ recommends controlling data permissions to prevent manipulation of business data that influences AI processing.
claims.quote: Make sure that your company has enough control over data permissions to ensure that business data can't be manipulated to influence AI data processing in an undesirable way.

claims.quote: Go to System administration > Setup > Demand planning app parameters. ... in the Demand planning app URL field, enter the URL where Demand planning is installed.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls: first table row
claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 admin center license-assignment path is Billing > Licenses > product > Assign licenses.
claims.quote: In the admin center, go to the Billing > Licenses page. ... Select a product. ... On the product details page, select Assign licenses.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls: first table row
claims.claim: POST /v1.0/users/{id | userPrincipalName}/assignLicense assigns or removes a user's licenses.
claims.quote: Add or remove licenses for the user ... POST /users/{id | userPrincipalName}/assignLicense ... addLicenses ... removeLicenses ... POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me/assignLicense
claims.fix: Keep the call unchanged. Add to controls[0].note and the rendered note: 'The request body uses addLicenses with skuId to assign licenses and removeLicenses to remove them.' The v1.0 reference documents the endpoint; the pre-check's literal-string miss is not an endpoint defect.

claims.claim: The admin-center assignment procedure requires at least License Administrator or User Administrator.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.

claims.claim: The Demand planning licensing page links both assignment pages identified in the briefing.
claims.quote: For details about how to assign licenses to users, see Assign licenses and Assign or unassign licenses for users in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls: second table row
claims.claim: The Power Platform admin center path is Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Users > user > Manage security roles.
claims.quote: select Manage. ... select Environments, and then select an environment ... Select Settings. ... Select Users + permissions, and then select Users. ... select a user, and then select Manage security roles.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls: second table row
claims.claim: The printed Dataverse v9.0 POST to systemuserroles_association/$ref assigns a security role to the identified user.

claims.claim: Assigning security roles requires System Administrator or the appropriate privileges documented on the assignment page.

claims.quote: Searched: "Demand planning license requirements" "Graph" "assignLicense"; read the licensing page in full and the Graph reference. The licensing page links assignment guidance but does not print or name the Graph call.
